title: Software Engineering
summary: A study path for building reliable applications, services, and digital systems.
description: Software engineering suits learners who enjoy solving problems, building useful tools, and improving systems over time. It combines programming, databases, testing, teamwork, and product thinking, with strong career options across many industries.
learningRoute: Learn programming fundamentals and basic web concepts.
Build small projects that use data storage and APIs.
Practice software design, testing, version control, and deployment.

title: Frontend Engineer
summary: Builds user-facing web interfaces that are useful, accessible, and pleasant to use.
description: Frontend engineering is a practical career for people who like both logic and visual detail. It involves translating designs and user needs into responsive interfaces, connecting to APIs, improving performance, and making digital products easy to understand.
learningRoute: Master HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and responsive layouts.
Build React projects connected to real API data.
Learn accessibility, performance, testing, and design-system basics.

title: Backend Engineer
summary: Builds APIs, data models, and server logic that power applications.
description: Backend engineering fits people who enjoy systems, data flow, and problem-solving behind the scenes. The work includes designing APIs, managing databases, securing services, and making applications reliable as usage grows.
learningRoute: Learn server-side programming and database fundamentals.
Create REST APIs with authentication and validation.
Study caching, security, testing, and deployment practices.

title: Mobile App Developer
summary: Creates mobile applications for everyday services, learning, business, and entertainment.
description: Mobile development is a strong option for builders who want their work to reach people directly on phones. It includes interface development, device features, offline behavior, app performance, and release workflows.
learningRoute: Learn JavaScript or a mobile-first language and app structure.
Build apps that use navigation, storage, and API calls.
Practice publishing, performance tuning, and user feedback cycles.

title: Data Analyst
summary: Turns raw data into clear findings that help teams make better decisions.
description: Data analysis fits analytical learners who like patterns, evidence, and practical business questions. The work often includes cleaning data, building dashboards, interpreting trends, and explaining what the numbers mean.
learningRoute: Learn spreadsheet analysis, SQL, and basic statistics.
Build dashboards from realistic datasets.
Practice explaining insights with charts and written recommendations.

title: Machine Learning Specialist
summary: Develops data-driven models for prediction, automation, and intelligent features.
description: Machine learning is best for people who enjoy math, experimentation, programming, and long-term learning. It requires patience with data quality, model evaluation, and translating technical results into useful applications.
learningRoute: Build strong foundations in Python, statistics, and linear algebra.
Train and evaluate supervised learning models on clean datasets.
Apply models in small applications and learn responsible AI practices.

title: Cybersecurity Analyst
summary: Protects systems by monitoring threats, investigating incidents, and improving defenses.
description: Cybersecurity analysis fits detail-oriented problem solvers who like investigation and structured procedures. The role combines networking basics, logs, risk thinking, communication, and continuous learning as threats change.
learningRoute: Learn computer networks, operating systems, and security fundamentals.
Practice log analysis, threat detection, and incident response labs.
Study cloud security, compliance basics, and clear reporting.

title: Information Technology Support
summary: Helps users and organizations keep computers, networks, and software working reliably.
description: IT support is a practical entry route into technology for people who like hands-on troubleshooting and helping others. It builds foundations in hardware, operating systems, networking, user support, and service processes.
learningRoute: Learn computer hardware, operating systems, and basic networking.
Practice diagnosing common software and connectivity issues.
Build service habits through ticketing, documentation, and user communication.

title: Nursing
summary: A clinical study path focused on patient care, health monitoring, and practical support.
description: Nursing suits people who are steady, organized, compassionate, and ready for hands-on clinical work. It requires science learning, communication, discipline, and the ability to support people during stressful moments.
learningRoute: Build foundations in biology, anatomy, and patient safety.
Practice clinical skills through supervised labs and placements.
Develop care planning, documentation, and teamwork habits.

title: Medical Laboratory Scientist
summary: Performs laboratory tests that support diagnosis, treatment, and public health.
description: Medical laboratory science fits careful, analytical people who like science but prefer structured lab work over constant public-facing care. The role demands accuracy, quality control, and respect for safety procedures.
learningRoute: Study biology, chemistry, and laboratory safety fundamentals.
Practice sample processing, microscopy, and diagnostic testing.
Learn quality systems, reporting, and equipment maintenance.

title: Public Health Officer
summary: Plans and supports programs that improve health outcomes for communities.
description: Public health is a strong match for people who care about prevention, community impact, and systems-level change. It blends health knowledge, communication, data, outreach, and program coordination.
learningRoute: Learn public health principles, prevention, and community assessment.
Practice designing outreach activities and simple health surveys.
Build skills in reporting, stakeholder coordination, and program evaluation.

title: Nutrition and Dietetics
summary: A health study path focused on food, wellbeing, prevention, and practical nutrition planning.
description: Nutrition and dietetics is useful for learners interested in science, people, and everyday health decisions. It can lead to clinical, community, sports, and wellness roles depending on training and local licensing requirements.
learningRoute: Study human biology, food science, and nutrition fundamentals.
Practice dietary assessment and culturally realistic meal planning.
Learn counseling, public education, and evidence-based recommendations.

title: Accounting
summary: A business study path for financial records, reporting, auditing, and controls.
description: Accounting is practical for organized learners who like structure, numbers, and responsibility. It offers stable options in nearly every sector and can grow into audit, finance, tax, compliance, or management roles.
learningRoute: Learn bookkeeping, financial statements, and spreadsheet skills.
Practice accounting cycles, reconciliations, and reporting cases.
Study audit, tax, ethics, and accounting software.

title: Financial Analyst
summary: Uses financial data to evaluate performance, plan budgets, and guide decisions.
description: Financial analysis suits people who enjoy numbers, business questions, and evidence-based recommendations. The work can include budgeting, forecasts, investment analysis, reporting, and advising managers.
learningRoute: Build foundations in accounting, finance, and spreadsheet modeling.
Practice budgets, forecasts, and performance analysis.
Learn valuation basics, scenario planning, and executive reporting.

title: Digital Marketing Specialist
summary: Plans online campaigns that help organizations reach, understand, and serve customers.
description: Digital marketing fits creative communicators who also like measuring results. It includes content, social media, search, email, advertising, analytics, and ongoing experiments to improve growth.
learningRoute: Learn audience research, copywriting, and digital channel basics.
Run small content, search, or social campaigns and track results.
Build reporting habits and improve campaigns through testing.

title: Product Manager
summary: Guides product decisions by connecting user needs, business goals, and technical delivery.
description: Product management is a hybrid path for organized communicators who enjoy problem-solving, prioritization, and teamwork. It is less about coding directly and more about deciding what should be built and why.
learningRoute: Learn product discovery, user research, and basic technology concepts.
Practice writing requirements, prioritizing features, and reading metrics.
Work with design and engineering on small product improvements.

title: Entrepreneurship and Small Business
summary: Builds the skills needed to launch, test, and grow small ventures.
description: Entrepreneurship fits self-directed learners who like building, selling, adapting, and taking responsibility for uncertain outcomes. It requires customer understanding, financial discipline, operations, and resilience.
learningRoute: Identify a real customer problem and test demand cheaply.
Learn pricing, cash flow, basic marketing, and service delivery.
Build repeatable operations and measure what improves growth.

title: Primary School Teacher
summary: Supports younger learners in literacy, numeracy, confidence, and classroom habits.
description: Primary teaching suits patient communicators who enjoy helping children grow step by step. The role requires planning, classroom management, subject basics, empathy, and consistent routines.
learningRoute: Study child development, core subjects, and teaching methods.
Practice lesson planning, classroom routines, and formative assessment.
Complete supervised teaching practice and reflect on learner progress.

title: STEM Teacher
summary: Teaches science, math, and practical problem-solving through clear instruction.
description: STEM teaching is a strong option for people who like science or math and also enjoy explaining ideas to others. It combines subject knowledge, demonstrations, assessment, and student motivation.
learningRoute: Build subject confidence in math, science, or technology.
Practice explaining concepts with examples and classroom activities.
Learn lab safety, assessment design, and differentiated instruction.

title: Instructional Designer
summary: Designs courses, training materials, and learning experiences for specific outcomes.
description: Instructional design suits organized creators who like explaining ideas clearly. The role can work in education, corporate training, NGOs, and online learning, often combining writing, design, assessment, and technology.
learningRoute: Learn learning objectives, curriculum structure, and assessment basics.
Create sample lessons, worksheets, and digital modules.
Practice evaluating learner feedback and improving materials.

title: Civil Engineering
summary: A study path for designing and improving buildings, roads, water systems, and infrastructure.
description: Civil engineering fits learners who enjoy math, practical problem-solving, and visible real-world impact. It requires technical discipline, site awareness, teamwork, and responsibility for public safety.
learningRoute: Build foundations in math, physics, drawing, and materials.
Practice surveying, structural calculations, and design software.
Learn construction management, safety, and infrastructure planning.

title: Structural Engineer
summary: Designs and checks structures so buildings and infrastructure can carry loads safely.
description: Structural engineering suits analytical people who enjoy math-heavy design and careful responsibility. It involves calculations, codes, materials, modeling software, site coordination, and clear technical documentation.
learningRoute: Strengthen statics, mechanics, materials, and structural analysis.
Practice design calculations and modeling in engineering software.
Learn local codes, site coordination, and review workflows.

title: Renewable Energy Technician
summary: Installs, maintains, and troubleshoots solar and other renewable energy systems.
description: This hands-on pathway fits people who like practical technical work, outdoor or mixed environments, and useful systems. It can begin through vocational training and grow into design, supervision, or energy project work.
learningRoute: Learn electrical safety, circuits, and renewable energy basics.
Practice installation, testing, and maintenance of solar systems.
Study system sizing, batteries, inverters, and field documentation.

title: Mechanical Engineering
summary: A study path for machines, energy, manufacturing, maintenance, and mechanical systems.
description: Mechanical engineering suits learners who enjoy physics, design, hands-on systems, and problem-solving. It opens pathways into manufacturing, energy, automotive, HVAC, maintenance, and product development.
learningRoute: Build foundations in math, physics, mechanics, and drawing.
Practice CAD, workshop skills, and machine component design.
Study thermodynamics, manufacturing, controls, and maintenance systems.

title: Graphic Designer
summary: Creates visual materials that communicate messages clearly across digital and print media.
description: Graphic design fits creative people who enjoy visual problem-solving, layout, color, typography, and brand communication. It rewards practice, portfolio building, feedback, and understanding client goals.
learningRoute: Learn design principles, typography, color, and layout.
Create posters, social media assets, brand concepts, and portfolio pieces.
Practice client briefs, feedback cycles, and production-ready files.

title: UX/UI Designer
summary: Designs digital interfaces that help users complete tasks clearly and comfortably.
description: UX/UI design is a hybrid creative and analytical path. It suits people who care about people, visual clarity, research, and digital products, and who can turn user needs into practical screens and flows.
learningRoute: Learn user research, interface patterns, and visual design foundations.
Create wireframes and prototypes for realistic app workflows.
Test designs with users and build a portfolio explaining decisions.

title: Journalist
summary: Researches, verifies, writes, and produces stories for public audiences.
description: Journalism suits curious communicators who like reading, writing, people, and public issues. It requires accuracy, ethics, interviewing, research, and the ability to make complex topics understandable.
learningRoute: Practice news writing, research, interviewing, and fact checking.
Build a portfolio of articles, audio, or video stories.
Learn media law, ethics, editing, and audience engagement.

title: Video Content Producer
summary: Plans, records, edits, and publishes video content for education, marketing, or media.
description: Video production fits creative builders who enjoy storytelling, visuals, editing, and practical production work. It can grow from social media content into documentary, brand, education, or commercial production.
learningRoute: Learn framing, lighting, sound, and simple story structure.
Produce short videos for real topics and edit them consistently.
Build a portfolio and improve through audience feedback and client briefs.

title: Law
summary: A study path for legal reasoning, rights, governance, advocacy, and dispute resolution.
description: Law suits learners who enjoy reading, structured argument, social issues, and careful communication. It requires discipline, ethical judgment, research, writing, and comfort with complex rules.
learningRoute: Build reading, writing, logic, and civic knowledge foundations.
Study legal systems, contracts, criminal law, and constitutional principles.
Practice legal research, drafting, advocacy, and case analysis.

title: Policy Analyst
summary: Researches public problems and recommends practical policy options.
description: Policy analysis fits analytical communicators interested in society, systems, and evidence-based change. It often involves research, stakeholder input, writing briefs, comparing options, and evaluating impact.
learningRoute: Study public policy, economics, law basics, and research methods.
Practice writing policy briefs using real evidence.
Learn program evaluation, stakeholder mapping, and clear recommendations.

title: Counselor
summary: Supports people with emotional, educational, or life challenges through structured guidance.
description: Counseling fits patient listeners who care about people and can stay calm with sensitive topics. It requires formal training, ethics, boundaries, communication, and referral judgment.
learningRoute: Study psychology foundations, communication, and human development.
Practice supervised listening, assessment, and case documentation.
Learn ethics, safeguarding, referral systems, and local practice requirements.

title: Social Worker
summary: Helps individuals and communities access support, protection, and practical services.
description: Social work suits people who want direct human impact and can manage complex social situations with empathy and structure. It blends assessment, advocacy, case management, and coordination with services.
learningRoute: Study social systems, psychology basics, rights, and community work.
Practice assessment, case notes, referrals, and safeguarding processes.
Build field experience through supervised community or NGO placements.

title: Environmental Scientist
summary: Studies environmental conditions and supports decisions that protect natural systems.
description: Environmental science fits people who like nature, science, fieldwork, and evidence-based problem-solving. The work may include sampling, data analysis, reporting, conservation, and advising projects on environmental risk.
learningRoute: Study biology, ecology, chemistry, and environmental systems.
Practice field sampling, data recording, and basic GIS mapping.
Learn environmental assessment, reporting, and conservation planning.

title: Agronomy Specialist
summary: Improves crop production through soil, seed, water, and field management decisions.
description: Agronomy is a practical pathway for people who like science, nature, fieldwork, and food security. It combines crop knowledge, observation, farmer communication, and applied problem-solving.
learningRoute: Study plant science, soil, water, and crop production basics.
Practice field observation, pest identification, and yield improvement planning.
Learn advisory communication, farm records, and sustainable practices.

title: Sustainable Agriculture Entrepreneur
summary: Builds farming or food ventures that balance productivity, market demand, and sustainability.
description: This hybrid pathway fits builders who like nature, business, and practical systems. It requires learning crop or livestock basics, customer needs, cost control, supply chains, and sustainable production habits.
learningRoute: Choose a realistic product or farm service and study local demand.
Learn production basics, input costs, pricing, and quality control.
Test small, track results, and improve operations before scaling.
